title: I have built a Battlefield-style browser shooter with Claude Code, here is how I work with it
author: normativecoder
selftext:
Hello everyone,

I have built Sectorlock, a free multiplayer shooter that runs in the browser. Red vs Blue conquest, soldier and ninja classes, an attack helicopter, an F-16, and since yesterday a bald eagle that the ninja throws at people.

Claude Code writes most of the code. I decide what goes in, play it, and say what feels wrong. It's a Go server at 60 ticks and a three.js client, around 140k lines now plus tests.

A few things that made it work for me:

1- A big CLAUDE.md. Every rule of the game and every system is written there, so a new session doesn't break something it doesn't know about. It's about 2000 lines now.

2- Claude tests in a real browser. It opens Chrome, plays the game against bots and looks at the screenshots before it says something is done. More than once the unit tests passed while the game was clearly broken.

3- I judge by playing, not by reading code. Example: the eagle worked, but it was so small on screen that I couldn't see it attacking. Only playing showed that.

No generated art. Everything is built in code, except the F-16 and the eagle, which are CC BY models. Textures and sounds are CC0.

Playable link: [https://sectorlock.com](https://sectorlock.com)

No download, no account, and bots fill the teams when it's quiet.

Happy to answer questions about the workflow.
